name: Livesey and Marsh variant effect predictor benchmark (2025 edition)
description: Ranks missense variant effect predictors by pairwise comparisons of their Spearman correlation with human deep mutational scanning data, and separately by pairwise AUROC on ClinVar pathogenic versus gnomAD missense variants.

attributes.version: Genome Biol 2025;26:104 (third edition, after Mol Syst Biol 2020 and 2023)
attributes.task: Missense variant effect prediction, ranked against functional assays and clinical labels
attributes.scope_note: 97 VEPs on 36 human DMS datasets (one score set per protein, at least 1000 single amino acid substitutions after removing ClinVar and gnomAD variants); 83 VEPs on 819 proteins with at least 10 ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic and 10 gnomAD v4.1 missense variants. Rank score is each VEP's average pairwise win rate against all other VEPs.
attributes.source_locator: Results 'New DMS datasets and VEPs', 'Comparison of VEP performance using DMS data', 'Performance of VEPs on clinical variant classification'; Methods
limitations: Rank scores are relative: they depend on which other VEPs are in the comparison and are not a per-VEP correlation or AUROC.
The earlier editions (Mol Syst Biol 2020;16:e9380 and 2023;19:e11474) used other DMS sets, VEP sets and, in 2020, another ranking method; they are not extracted here.

name: Livesey and Marsh 2025 clinical benchmark: pairwise AUROC win rate, ClinVar pathogenic versus gnomAD missense
description: Rank score of each VEP from per-protein pairwise AUROC comparisons on 819 proteins (Table S8 rank_score).

attributes.scope_note: For each protein with at least 10 ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic and 10 gnomAD v4.1 missense variants, the AUROC of each pair of VEPs is compared on variants scored by both; the higher AUROC wins. Win rates across proteins are averaged over all other VEPs. No training variants were removed, so clinical-trained VEPs can benefit from circularity.
attributes.metric_qualifier: average pairwise win rate against all other VEPs, per-protein AUROC on shared variants, ClinVar P/LP versus gnomAD v4.1 missense, proteins with at least 10 of each
attributes.metric_implementation: sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score (sklearn 0.18.1); scores of VEPs where low means pathogenic are inverted by subtracting from 1; the higher AUROC on shared variants earns the point
attributes.aggregation: Win rate of each VEP pair across proteins (wins divided by times the pair was tested), averaged over all other VEPs (Methods, 'Spearman's correlation and rank score')
attributes.version: Livesey and Marsh 2025, Supplementary Material 2 Table S8
attributes.source_locator: Methods 'Spearman's correlation and rank score' and 'AUROC and AUPRC'; Supplementary Material 2 Legends (Table S8)
limitations: A rank score is relative to the other VEPs in the same table; values from different tables or editions are not comparable.
Per-pair, per-protein correlations and AUROCs behind the win rates are not printed; they are in the figshare deposit, which was not retrieved.
Clinical-trained VEPs were not filtered for training overlap; the authors attribute most of their advantage here to circularity (Results, Fig. 4).
Figure 3 error bars are the standard error across comparisons; they are not printed.
